comments.body:
## Measured: the liveness rule is inconsistent across relations, and BOTH of P6's remedies are refused

Filing this ticket produced the comparison for free. Against closed tickets, on the same
store, in the same minute:

| Attempted link | Endpoint that is closed | Result |
|---|---|---|
| `0461 --depends_on--> 2041` | target | **REFUSED** — "target ticket is closed" |
| `2041 --blocks--> 0461` | source | **REFUSED** — "source ticket is closed. Reopen it first with: `ticket transition 2041 closed open`" |
| `1544 --relates_to--> 868c` | target | ok |
| `1544 --relates_to--> 266e` | target | ok |
| `1544 --discovered_from--> 0461` | — (open) | ok |

Two things this settles.

**1. The link layer does not apply one liveness rule.** `relates_to` accepts a closed target
without complaint; `depends_on` refuses one. Nothing about the two relations justifies the
split — if anything the case for allowing it is stronger for `depends_on`, which records a
real ordering between two pieces of work, than for `relates_to`, which records only that
someone found them relevant to each other. So the defect is not "`depends_on` forgot to allow
closed targets"; it is that endpoint liveness is decided relation by relation with no stated
rule, so each relation's behaviour is whatever its own code path happened to do. `868c` is the
same thing on `supersedes`/closed-source. That is 3 relations with 3 answers and no table.

**2. `P6`'s constructive remedies are both unavailable, not just one.** The criterion offers
three: add `depends_on`, ensure the cited ticket `blocks` this one, or remove the citation.
The first two are the same edge seen from either end, and both are refused the moment the
upstream ticket merges. Only "remove the citation" survives — discarding accurate provenance
to satisfy a tool. So a plan that builds on MERGED work can never ground its citation to the
ticket that delivered that work, which is the case where the citation is most certainly
correct.

The `blocks` refusal also suggests its own remedy: "Reopen it first." Reopening a merged,
verified, closed ticket in order to record that later work depends on it would corrupt the
tracker's record of what is done to work around a link-layer rule.

## Not a blocker for 0461

`P6` is advisory (`decision: advisory`, `severity: minor`, `impact: 0.4`), so 0461's review is
not held by this. The cost is narrower and worth stating precisely: the citation to the ticket
that delivered the code 0461 builds on is "grounded as normal (fails closed)" instead of as a
verified prerequisite. The review still runs; it just cannot use the strongest evidence
available to it.

## Unverified

Whether `duplicates` and `caused_by` enforce liveness, and on which endpoint, has not been
measured. The fix's table needs all 6 relations, not the 4 observed here.

compiled_state.description:
## What happened

`rebar link 0461-09ce-4850-42a7 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9 depends_on` was refused:

```
Error: cannot create depends_on link — target ticket '2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9' is closed
```

2041 is closed because it MERGED. 0461 builds directly on the embedding tier 2041 delivered,
and 0461's plan cites `[rebar:2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9]` for exactly that reason.

## Why the refusal is wrong

Depending on completed work is the normal and desirable case. A `depends_on` edge records
"this work rests on that work"; the dependency is MORE certain once the target has landed,
not less. The refusal makes the edge expressible only during the window when the target is
still open — that is, only while the dependency is unproven — and permanently unexpressible
afterwards.

The practical damage is that the plan-review gate asks for precisely this edge and the store
refuses to create it. The `P6` criterion emits:

> citation `[rebar:2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9]` names no VERIFIED upstream prerequisite: P neither
> declares `depends_on -> 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9` nor is blocked by it. Add a `depends_on` edge
> to 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9, ensure 2041-75d6-2a2f-4be9 `blocks` this ticket, or remove the
> citation. Until then the cited symbol is grounded as normal (fails closed).

All 3 remedies are unavailable or wrong:

1. `depends_on` — refused by this defect.
2. `blocks` — the mirror of the same edge, and a closed ticket blocking an open one is both
   refused and semantically false.
3. "remove the citation" — discards accurate provenance to satisfy a tool, which inverts the
   purpose of grounding.

So any plan that builds on merged work is structurally unable to ground its citation to the
ticket that delivered that work. It is advisory rather than blocking today, so it degrades
review quality rather than halting work — but it degrades it on exactly the citations most
likely to be correct.

## Relation to 868c-dd56-d464-44bf

`868c` (`unpaid-sanctified-aardvark`) is the same class seen on a different edge: `supersedes`
refuses a CLOSED SOURCE while the disposition-close path that consumes those links accepts
one. This ticket is a closed TARGET on `depends_on`. Both are the link layer applying an
open-ticket liveness rule to a relation whose meaning does not require liveness. Whether the
fix is one shared predicate or per-relation rules is for the plan to decide; what should not
survive is 2 relations independently guessing.

## Suggested direction (not yet a plan)

Establish per-relation which endpoints legitimately require a live ticket. A blocking relation
plausibly does; a provenance or dependency-record relation plausibly does not. Then make the
link layer consult that table rather than applying one liveness rule to every relation.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `rebar link <open> <closed> depends_on` succeeds, and `rebar ticket-deps <open>` reports the edge.
- [ ] A closed `depends_on` target does NOT make the source unready: `rebar ready` still returns the source when its only unmet edge is a closed `depends_on` target.
- [ ] The plan-review `P6` criterion accepts a `depends_on` edge to a closed target as a VERIFIED upstream prerequisite, proved by a review over a fixture plan citing a closed ticket.
- [ ] The relation/endpoint liveness rules are stated in one place that both `supersedes` and `depends_on` consult, rather than per-relation branches, OR the plan records why per-relation rules are correct.
- [ ] A test pins each relation's endpoint-liveness rule, so a future relation cannot silently inherit the wrong one.
- [ ] `make verify` passes.

## Testing

A unit test per relation/endpoint pair over the link layer, plus one plan-review fixture test
proving `P6` is satisfied by an edge to a closed target. No live provider call is needed for
either.

## Out of scope

Changing what `blocks` means for a closed ticket, and any change to the disposition-close path
that `868c` already covers.
compiled_state.title: depends_on refuses a closed target, so a plan cannot ground a citation to completed work
